summaryDeep: Their idealism, vagueness, and dreams press against your thinking and how you talk and decide. It catches often enough that you both feel it, and it keeps asking to be worked out. Name it directly instead of letting it build in silence.
tension: It is rarely actual lying, though it can feel that way. More often it is perception. You hear something confusing, decide they must be hiding something, and only realize later that they were clear the first time and you understood it in a completely different light. The tell is that they communicate with everyone else fine. The problem lives between the two of you, and the closer the aspect, the worse it gets. The distrust is often baseless, and it tends to come from the Neptune person. Left alone, the Mercury person gets tired of being doubted and walks away. This does not break in a single dramatic moment. Trust erodes gradually, through a slow build-up of misunderstandings, half-truths, and well-meant vagueness, until the pattern is entrenched before either of you sees it. What makes it hard is that the square makes honest communication feel uncomfortable and dishonest communication feel natural. Clarity feels harsh. Vagueness feels kind. Specificity feels aggressive. These associations are backwards, and recognizing that they are backwards is the first step toward fixing the dynamic.
advice: It can be worked through. Say what you mean in plain language, even when it feels unromantic. When something does not make sense, ask about it directly instead of filling in the blanks. Be transparent with each other. The trust problem can be repaired when both of you do your part.
summaryShort: Their idealism, vagueness, and dreams press against your thinking and how you talk and decide.
